She calls making herself needed the biggest theme of her life, yet builds her songs on sadness and longing. Her interview record, nearly all from 2025-26 promotion, can't yet separate them.
findings.problem: The type thesis changed after the frozen review. All six roles reviewed a draft whose leading read was Type 4 (draft.md enneagram '4'; evidence-draft type_hypothesis.type 4). The edit moved the lead to Type 2 in enneagram, title, meta_title, description, persona_title, the 60-word answer, the FAQs, type_hypothesis and open_case. It also set risks.major_thesis_change, which no reviewer flagged. fan-01, critic-01 and enneagram-02 asked for or allowed this, but their own acceptance tests say a lead change must hold for --refresh --expanded-review, and the resolution says the edit does not absorb it. No independent reviewer has yet challenged the Two-led argument as written: its recurrence count (verify-02), its clinging/helping split (verify-03), or whether the longing pattern is better read as Four. On the opened record the Two lead looks defensible to me (SSENSE November 2025, Z100 March 2026, Capital April 2026, Zach Sang June 2026), but that does not replace the required jury.
findings.acceptance_test: The run is resumed with scripts/run-blog-pipeline.sh Sienna-Spiro --refresh --expanded-review. findings.passage: The Two case rests on her most explicit self-description, returned to in at least five interviews between November 2025 and June 2026: she made herself needed because she didn't think people would want her otherwise.
findings.problem: The colon makes the five interviews repeat a specific belief. Only SSENSE (November 2025: 'nobody really wanted to be around me ... overcompensating and giving a lot of myself') and Z100 (March 2026: 'I had to make myself like needed ... I never thought people would want me otherwise if they didn't need me') state it. Genius (February 2026: mirroring 'to be kept around'), Capital (April 2026: if she stopped initiating, friendships 'wouldn't happen') and Zach Sang (June 2026: 'I give a lot of myself ... taken advantage of') describe related conditional belonging or giving without that belief. The count overstates the strongest Two evidence.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence separates the two explicit statements from the three related ones (for example 'stated outright in November 2025 and March 2026 and echoed in three more 2026 interviews'), or drops the count. C84's inference says the same.

findings.passage: So the change she describes runs from clinging, to closing off, to letting things end. The helping is the one part she never describes dropping.
findings.problem: In Z100 (March 2026, ~08:58-11:27) she first describes always calling, texting, 'making the effort' and being the therapist friend. She then says she would 'hold on so tightly or be too much' that people left, and that she 'had to learn how to not be like that because it's actually exhausting.' The referent of 'like that' can include the over-giving, not only clinging. 'What she says she has changed is something else' and 'never describes dropping' therefore read one ambiguous referent one way. The three-stage order is also the article's synthesis across interviews, not her own sequence. The Two lead does not depend on this sentence (it rests on the 2026 present-tense statements), but the hinge claims more than the transcript shows.
findings.acceptance_test: The hinge says what the record supports without the absolute, for example that she never clearly describes dropping the helping and still described it in the present tense in June 2026. Or it notes that her March 2026 'not be like that' may cover being 'too much' as well as clinging. The C53 and C11 inferences record the ambiguity.

findings.passage: On July 8, 2026, she put the new stance to [Z100](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aJRofzOtKmg): "So be it. Allow it to end. Like if you don't want me, don't have me."
findings.problem: July 8, 2026 is the video's YouTube upload date (yt-dlp metadata 20260708), not an established recording date. The same applies to 'she told [Billboard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FknTvkR0FmY) on October 2, 2026' (upload 20261002). Stating an upload day as the day she spoke adds precision the source doesn't establish.
findings.acceptance_test: Both sentences use the month ('In July 2026', 'in October 2026') or say 'in a video published on ...'. The S19 and S15 locators record that the date is the upload date.

findings.passage: "The Visitor" is about "knowing you're temporary to someone," she said on [TODAY in Australia](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e5I8NTEnrQw) in April 2026, "and knowing you probably care about that person more than they care about you."
findings.problem: In the audio (TODAY ~02:24-02:37, confirmed by my Whisper pass) the two fragments are separated by 'And this like fear of impermanence'. The article splits the quotation around the attribution so they read as adjacent, with no marker for the omitted phrase. The meaning is unchanged, but the adjacency is implied rather than true. Separately, in 'I'm a very loyal and I can be very valuable to some people' (Z100, July 2026, ~14:48), the captions have 'can' but my independent Whisper pass hears 'could'. It is one word with the same meaning, but it is unresolved.
findings.acceptance_test: The TODAY fragment either includes the omitted phrase or the gap is marked, for example 'and, she added, "knowing you probably care ..."'. The Z100 'can'/'could' is settled by a human listen, or only the shared words are printed (for example 'very loyal' ... 'very valuable to some people'). No other split quotation implies adjacency the source lacks.

findings.problem: checkDraft counts about 3,280 words, roughly 30% over the open-case target of about 1,200-2,500. The standard says not to pad a thin record. The drive section and the limits section carry the most outlet-by-outlet attribution and process detail, and the orientation paragraph stacks chart facts. Pace suffers more than the argument.
